# The Multiplier column means two opposite things

**Status:** Classes A and B fixed and shipped. Classes C, D and E are recorded here and NOT fixed.
**Scope:** Teltonika AVL dictionaries only (`packages/codec/dictionaries/*.json`, generated by
`tools/avl-dict`). **Owner of the decisions:** `tools/avl-dict/src/corrections.ts`.

## The defect

Teltonika's per-model "Data Sending Parameters" tables carry a **Multiplier** cell and a **Units**
cell, and the relationship between them is not fixed:

| id | table | Units | Multiplier | what `raw × multiplier` is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10879 High voltage battery voltage | fmc650 | `mV` | `50` | **millivolts** — the cell describes the RESULT |
| 67 Battery Voltage | fmm650 | `mV` | `0,001` | **volts** — the cell describes the RAW WIRE VALUE |

Nothing in the row distinguishes them. `apps/web/src/lib/telemetry.ts` multiplied and then applied
its own SI rescale keyed on the Units cell, so the second kind was divided by a thousand **twice**:

```
12600 (wire)  ×0.001 → 12.6  →  mV→V rescale → 0.0126  →  rendered "0.0 V"
```

A healthy 12.6 V backup battery therefore read as **`0.0 V`** — the exact reading of dead hardware —
beside a health chart showing 12.6 V computed from the same number. The premise that shipped it is
still in the file's history: *"mV is a thousandth of a volt on every table in the world, so scaling
it needs no knowledge of the element."* True of the **unit**. False of this **cell**.

## The proof that needs no wiki

Id 67 carries multiplier `0,001` on six generated dictionaries. `fmc650.json` says `units: "V"`;
`fmm650`, `fmc640`, `fmb641`, `fmb640` and `fm6300` say `"mV"` — same element, same multiplier, same
FMX6XX silicon. The identical raw value rendered **12.6 V on an FMC650 and 0.0 V on an FMM650**, side
by side in one product. That is a contradiction inside this repository, and only one of the two
readings produces a voltage a battery can have.

## The fix

`units` stays **verbatim** — it is provenance and answers *"what did the wiki say?"*. A derived
field answers the only question arithmetic may ask:

```
unitAfterMultiplier   absent  → the Units cell IS the post-multiplier unit; read `unitAfterMultiplier ?? units`
                      string  → it is not, and this is
                      null    → REFUSED; no unit may be claimed, show the number bare
```

Every emitted row also carries `unitSource` (the bare wiki URL that settled it — rule 8 travels with
the artifact) and `unitRule` (which of the four decisions below made it). The ARGUMENT stays in
`corrections.ts`: 57 copies of four paragraphs was 24 KB of prose in the dictionaries, fourteen times
the size of the field it explained, and it embedded internal repository paths in files that ship
inside a white-label product.

The generator **refuses to write any dictionary** while one ambiguous row is undecided, and names
every one of them across every table in a single message. Ambiguous means: the Units cell is
SI-prefixed (`mV mA mm ml mG mg`) **and** the multiplier actually scales.

**Say the scope out loud: 1,354 corpus rows carry a scaling multiplier and this guard polices 57 of
them.** It is not "every row whose multiplier might be misread" — it is the rows where a READER
rescales on the unit's own prefix and would therefore apply the factor twice. A multiplier that is
simply *wrong* is a different defect, and the live example is in "What is NOT fixed" below. A multiplier that is
exactly `1` is a no-op and needs no decision (18 rows); a multiplier that cannot be READ (`0.01*`,
`acc and braking: 0.01` — 129 cells in the corpus) counts as scaling, because an unreadable factor
is the last thing to assume harmless.

Corrections are keyed on **(table, id), never on id alone**. Ids collide across families and not
only between two measurements: **id 327 is "UL202-02 Sensor Fuel level" on the FMB1XX tables and
"Geofence zone 21" on the FMX6XX ones**; 224 and 225 are ultrasonic fuel levels on one family and
geofence zones 43/44 on the other. An id-keyed correction would have given a geofence flag a unit in
millimetres.

## What was decided — 11 elements, 57 rows

### Class A — the cell names the PRE-multiplier unit (18 rows CORRECTED)

| ids | tables | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 6, 9 Analog Input 1/2 | fmb010 fmb150 fmc150 fmc250 fmm150 fmm80a | the master template and ~20 sibling pages write `V` for the byte-identical row; ids 66/67 on the SAME page share the geometry `2 \| Unsigned \| 0 \| 65535 \| 0.001` and are published as `V`; the hardware measures 0–10 V / 0–30 V, so a literal mV reading tops out at 65.535 mV — under one percent of the input's own range. Traccar reads id 9 as `readUnsignedShort() / 1000.0`. |
| 66, 67 External/Battery Voltage | fm6300 (66, 67); fmb640 fmb641 fmc640 fmm650 (67) | Teltonika corrected it themselves: `Template:FMX650_AVL_ID` publishes the identical id-67 row as `0,001 \| V` for exactly FMB640/FMC640/FMM640/FMC650/FMM650. The pages still reading mV transclude one stale template. The back-up battery is Ni-MH 8.4–10.0 V; under the literal reading its full scale would be 30 mV. |

Honest caveat: Traccar registers no handler for id 6 (its `adc2` is id 10), so id 6 rests on the
wiki rows and the cross-model majority rather than on the oracle.

### Class B — the cell already describes the result (39 rows CONFIRMED)

| ids | tables | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 10879, 10880, 10886, 10887 EV pack / EVSE | fmb641 fmc640 fmc650 fmm650 | `raw × 50` millivolts is how a 400 V traction pack is reported (8000 → 400 000 mV → 400.0 V). |
| 10901, 10902 Highest / Lowest cell voltage | fmb641 fmc640 fmc650 fmm650 | declared, but **nothing is emitted for them**: their multiplier is `1`, so the cell describes raw and result alike and the guard never asks. They are written down because a reader who checks the ×50 rows will look for them; the 39 emitted rows do not include these 8. |
| 224, 225 Ultrasonic Fuel Level 1/2 | fm6300 fmb640 fmb641 fmc640 fmc650 fmm650 | the UL202's own front panel displays the level to one decimal **in millimetres**: `000.0` uncoupled, and *"the predicted level is about 300mm and displayed 285.2mm"* once installed. `285.2 mm` on the panel is `2852` on the wire, so `× 0.1` IS the millimetre figure. Tank height is set in **centimetres** on the same panel (`F030` = 30 cm), so a centimetre result would overshoot any tank the probe fits by 100×. |
| 327 UL202-02 Sensor Fuel level | fmb001 fmb010 fmb120 fmb150 fmb930 fmc150 fmc250 fmc880 fmm150 fmm80a fmm880 | same sensor, same reasoning. |

Class B carried no display bug — the browser rescales `mV` and `mA` and has no rule for `mm`. It is
declared anyway because the guard cannot tell the harmless case from the `0.0 V` case, and being
made to decide is the entire point of the guard.

Sources: <https://wiki.teltonika-gps.com/view/UL202_Ultrasonic_Fuel_Sensor>,
<https://wiki.teltonika-gps.com/view/Template:FMX650_AVL_ID>,
<https://wiki.teltonika-gps.com/view/FMB150_Teltonika_Data_Sending_Parameters_ID>.

## What is NOT fixed

These are real and separate; none of them is the `0.0 V` shape, and each needs its own evidence pass.

* **Class C — the UNITS CELL itself encodes a factor.** `10*°C` (42 entries), `10*Bar` (26) and
  `10*t` (2) are not units; they are instructions written where a unit goes. Nothing reads them
  today, so a pressure shows as a bare number rather than a wrong one — and `unitAfterMultiplier`
  deliberately does not touch them, because they are a second, different ambiguity.
* **Class D — offset encodings.** 28 distinct elements (34 rows, almost all on `tft100`) carry a
  documented negative minimum on an **Unsigned** field: `−40..210` coolant temperature, `−125..125`
  percent torque, `−273..1734.96875` J1939 exhaust temperatures. That is the SAE J1939 offset
  signature, which no multiplier can express. The generator warns on every one of them, and
  `applySign` refuses to sign-extend them (a raised floor is not a sign bit) — but **nothing
  subtracts the offset**, so those values are shown as the raw counts they are.
* **Class E — footnoted multipliers.** ~129 cells are not numbers (`0.01*`, `0.1*`,
  `acc and braking: 0.01`). `parseMultiplier` refuses them, so the value is shown exactly as the
  device sent it — honest, and not yet right.
* **Class F — the MULTIPLIER itself is wrong, or contradicts another table. This one is live.**
  Five `(id, name, units)` triples carry different multipliers on different tables:

  | id | element | units | the split | ratio |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 66 | External Voltage | `V` | `×0.001` on 19 tables, **`×0.01` on fmb930** | 10× |
  | 56 | Absolute Fuel Rail Pressure | `kPa` | `×0.1` on 7 tables, `×10` on fmb001/fmb010/fmb120 | 100× |
  | 72, 73, 74 | Dallas Temperature 1–3 | `°C` | `×0.1` on 25 tables, `×10` on fm36 | 100× |

  **fmb930 id 66 is a defect a customer can see today.** Teltonika's own page says *"FMB930 shows
  external voltage 10 times lower than it actually is. Multiply the value by 10 at the backend"*, so
  the effective factor is `0.01 × 10 = 0.1`. `packages/db/src/health.ts:73` does exactly that and
  cites the note; the parameters tab applies the dictionary's `0.01` and nothing else. One stored
  reading of 126 therefore renders **`1.3 V` in the parameters list and `12.6 V` on the health chart
  of the same device page** — the same "a number disagreeing with a chart about itself" this document
  opens with, arriving through the multiplier instead of the unit. `unitAfterMultiplier` structurally
  cannot express it: the unit is right and the factor is wrong.
  *Next change, and the reason it is not this one: the honest fix makes the dictionary the single
  source for that factor, which means `health.ts`, `fuel.ts`, `can.ts` and the rule engine stop
  carrying their own per-table constants — four surfaces, none of them the display layer.*
* **The display layer is the ONLY consumer.** `packages/db/src/health.ts`, `packages/db/src/fuel.ts`,
  `packages/db/src/can.ts` and the rule engine in `apps/worker/src/rules/` each hardcode their own
  factor plus a per-table exception list and never open a dictionary. The motivating story at the top
  of this document — "beside a health chart showing 12.6 V" — is two hardcodings that happen to
  agree, not a contract. Declare a refusal or a non-0.001 landing for id 67 on any table and the
  parameters tab goes quiet while the alert e-mail still asserts volts, with nothing to detect it.
  Class F above cannot be fixed without fixing this, which is why they are one follow-up and not two.
* **Model-gated tables.** `fmb120` and `fmb640` share 266 ids and disagree about the name of 213 of
  them (216 before case-folding; 226 once bytes, units and multiplier are compared too), and the
  model is not on the wire. Tracked separately.
* **Capitalisation.** The wiki is inconsistent about it and two layers take it literally: 7 tables
  carry names that differ only in case (`Fuel Level`/`Fuel level` on fmb120, `Throttle
  Position`/`Throttle position` on four), which the pipeline's same-name guard does not treat as the
  same name; and 19 element names go untranslated in lt/pl/de for no reason but a capital letter.
  Both predate this change. Tracked separately.

## Checked and found sound

Recorded so the next pass does not re-litigate them:

* **`m` with a scaling multiplier** — ids 12401 "Ground based distance" and 12404 "Wheel based
  distance" (`m`, `×0.001`) on fmb641/fmc650/fmm650. The reader rescales metres to kilometres for
  distance counters, so a misread here would be 1000× wide. It is not one: the documented maximum is
  `4211081215` = `0xFAFFFFFF`, the J1939 largest-valid value for a 4-byte parameter, and `0.001` is
  the RESOLUTION expressed in the stated unit (1 mm = 0.001 m). The cell describes the result. Full
  scale is 4211.08 km, which is what we render.
* **The six `m` rows on fm36** (LVCAN arm geometry, `×0.1`/`×0.01`) are not distance counters, so no
  metre→kilometre rescale reaches them.

## Adding a declaration

1. Run `pnpm --filter @orbetra/avl-dict gen`. If it refuses, it names every undecided row.
2. Open that row's own wiki page and settle it — the Min/Max cells, the same page's sibling rows,
   the hardware's physical range, and Traccar's decoder are the four things that usually decide it.
3. Add it to `tools/avl-dict/src/corrections.ts` with `rule` (a short name for the decision),
   `reason` (one sentence a reviewer can check) and `source` (a bare wiki URL). Rule 8 applies: a
   correction without a citation is a guess with better formatting. If it genuinely cannot be
   settled, declare `{ kind: 'refuse' }` — the value is then shown with no unit at all, which is
   honest and is tested (a refused row draws no percentage bar and carries no unit label).

   There is deliberately **no `--allow-undeclared`**. The sibling guards are more forgiving for
   reasons that do not apply: `--allow-remap` exists because a template split is a real event a human
   confirms, and the shrink guard is local to one page. An undeclared row is a question with an
   answer one wiki row away, and the only way to "allow" it is to guess — the silent default that
   shipped `0.0 V` in the first place.
4. Re-run the generator and `turbo run test --filter=@orbetra/codec`.
